topics.label: Opening framing: complement’s importance and difficulty
topics.groupedBecause: This opening welcomes the audience and frames complement as an important but difficult subject.

topics.label: Overview of complement’s activation and roles
topics.groupedBecause: This overview establishes the basic framework for complement activation and explains its broad role in immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature and its exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions for complement components and the exceptions that make them confusing.

topics.label: C3 activation and the functions of C3a and C3b
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic presents C3 as the central complement component and explains what its cleavage products do.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the recognition pathways deposit C3 and how their activity can build to the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Downstream effects of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement carries out its downstream effects on pathogens and the immune response.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and protection of host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins limit complement activation on host cells and prevent damage to them.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in complement components and regulators to their distinct clinical consequences.

topics.label: Staphylococcal complement evasion and uses of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic shows how Staphylococcus aureus evades complement and how protein A’s antibody binding is used in clinical and laboratory settings.

topics.label: Closing and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture, thanks the audience, and signals the next lecture.
